clue.text: Bird dog gets punishment for picking up party food

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the thing rather than a noun

blocks.note: a cock is a male bird
to dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail them
giving someone stick means punishing or criticising them

explanation.surface: A bird dog is disciplined for snaffling the canapés at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird dog' reads as a gun dog, but the two words split: a bird and a verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail stick is the small wooden spike used to spear olives and sausages at drinks parties.

the Roman numeral for one

clue.text: King acquires fine forged blade

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written

clue.text: Prevent rave being organised on edge of town

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to ward it off or stop it happening.

clue.text: Book-keeper taking over incomplete account managed to take quality up

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing its end, so the final letter goes
turned over, so the shortened word is read from right to left
the first word takes the next one inside it, enclosing it
in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: a bill is an account of money owed
to run a business is to manage it
an air is a quality or manner, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: An accountant takes over unfinished books and manages to raise their standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book-keeper' suggests an accountant, which the surface plays up, but it means someone who keeps books in a library. The two reversal signals work on different pieces: 'over' on the shortened account, 'up' on the quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian looks after a library's collection, literally keeping books, a playful twist on the accounting job.

clue.text: Let cop see suspect contract

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Allow the policeman to inspect a suspicious contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, a document, but it is the verb: to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To telescope is to shorten or compress, like the sliding tubes of the instrument closing up.

explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a statement of the beliefs someone holds.

clue.text: Royal pair made nice company at first — natural and kind

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The prince consort is a member of the royal family by marriage, so he is a royal.

clue.text: Mature splendidly indeed, love playing part initially

the word read without its first two letters
taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, to have being, so it matches live as a verb.
